title: Human Rights and Responsibilities
summary: The Constitution and the Bill of Rights, important rights and the responsibilities that come with them, children's rights, human rights violations and institutions that protect rights.

notes.text: The Constitution and the Bill of Rights

The **Constitution of the Republic of South Africa (1996)** is the **highest law** of the country. All other laws and the actions of government must agree with it. Chapter 2 of the Constitution is the **Bill of Rights**, which protects the rights of **everyone** in South Africa.

notes.label: Founding values
notes.text: The Constitution is based on **human dignity**, **equality** and **freedom**, non-racialism and non-sexism, and the rule of law.

Every right comes with a **responsibility**: we must respect the same rights of other people. Rights can also be **limited** when they clash with the rights of others; for example, freedom of expression does not include hate speech.

rows: Equality (s 9)
Treat everyone fairly; do not discriminate
Human dignity (s 10)
Respect other people; do not humiliate or bully
Life (s 11)
Do not harm others; drive safely
Freedom and security of the person (s 12)
Do not use violence against anyone
Privacy (s 14)
Do not read others' messages or share their personal information
Freedom of expression (s 16)
Do not spread hate speech or lies about others
Environment (s 24)
Do not litter or pollute; save water and energy
Education (s 29)
Attend school, work hard and allow others to learn

items: A name and nationality from birth.
Family care or appropriate alternative care.
Basic nutrition, shelter, health care and social services.
Protection from **maltreatment, neglect, abuse** and degradation.
Protection from **child labour** and exploitative work.
A child's **best interests** are of paramount importance in every matter concerning the child.

notes.text: A **human rights violation** happens when someone's rights are ignored or abused, for example racism and discrimination, gender-based violence (GBV), child abuse, xenophobic attacks on foreign nationals, bullying, or denying someone access to education or healthcare.

rows: South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC)
Investigates human rights violations and educates the public
Constitutional Court
The highest court on constitutional matters; can strike down laws that conflict with the Constitution
Public Protector
Investigates abuse of power and corruption by government officials
Commission for Gender Equality
Promotes gender equality and investigates gender discrimination
SAPS (police) and courts
Enforce laws and protect people from crime

notes.text: Ordinary citizens also protect rights by speaking out, reporting abuse, voting, joining campaigns and treating others with respect.
